claims.text: Under ADR 0029 signing depends on three outside services: the provider's HSM, a timestamp authority and the CA (OCSP responder or CRL); the review's step 5 calls each a single point of failure for signing, not for taking orders or refunds.
When the HSM, TSA or CA fails (for the CA: no status from the responder or the CRL), the statement waits and is retried within a few hours (assumed); orders and refunds are not affected.
A statement may wait a few hours to be signed (assumed) without breaking a driver, as long as it meets the bank's deadline, the fifth working day of the next month (assumed).

The design review records the OCSP/CRL trade-off point: OCSP gives a fresh answer about one certificate but needs the responder up at each query; a CRL can be fetched ahead and kept, but may be as old as one publishing interval.

ADR 0029 fetches the revocation status at signing time by asking the CA's OCSP responder first, and uses the CA's CRL when there is no responder; it does not say whether a responder that is down counts as none.
Saving the status at signing makes the package larger than a bare signature, but the bank's check years later (10 years, assumed) needs no CA service still running.

The trusted timestamp is signed by the TSA, whose certificate also ends; ADR 0029 gives stored packages a new timestamp before it does, without redoing the signature (Ý kiến đã nhận), a recurring job recorded as a cost.

claims.text: ADR 0029 signs with a key in ADR 0023's provider HSM used only for this bank's statements (the invoice key sits in that HSM per ADR 0023); revoking it touches no invoice, at the cost of one more key and certificate.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0029 (docs/adr/0029-ky-bang-ke-...) @ stage-4 lines 37-39, 55; docs/design/bank-signing-design-review.md lines 81-82; ADR 0023 title

claims.text: Stage-4 has no code that signs bank statements; ADR 0029's header says so.
Review step 5 finds no load bottleneck (at most a few hundred statements a month, assumed).
Rejected: server time and an own root (bank trusts only a root it names; a leaked key could set server time before revocation; drivers 1, 2); own HSM (ADR 0023; ADR 0022 reopen); shared invoice key.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/bank-signing-design-review.md @ stage-4 lines 72-75; docs/adr/0029-... Các phương án; docs/team/bank-signing-requirements.md Giả định

claims.text: ADR 0023 rejects an own HSM (which gives full control of the hardware) because it needs devices in two places so one site failing does not stop signing, and people to operate, upgrade and back them up.

ADR 0029 is revisited when a contract demands the key on own machines (reopen condition of ADR 0022 and 0023; a new ADR then replaces ADR 0023 for that key only), when the bank demands its own signature format, or when a second bank needs statements.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0029 (docs/adr/0029-ky-bang-ke-...) @ stage-4 lines 61-63; ADR 0022 line 78; ADR 0023 lines 47-49

claims.text: Ranked drivers: (1) checkable for years (10, assumed), even after the certificate ends; (2) a leaked key's damage limited in time; (3) no key outside an HSM. The requirements list, for the product owner to confirm, that the contract does not demand own-machine HSM.

claims.text: If signing had to finish within seconds inside a request a customer waits on, the three services would sit on that path and the trade-offs would need weighing again.
claims.source_hint: derived from review lines 66-68 and ADR 0029 lines 48-49

claims.text: Under a contract demanding own machines, a new ADR replaces 0023 for the bank key only; the other keys do not change, and ADR 0022's reopen condition is also met, so that decision is looked at again. Weighing it is a total-cost question.
claims.source_hint: derived from ADR 0029 lines 61-63, ADR 0023 lines 47-49, ADR 0022 line 78; management.l3.total-cost-of-ownership

claims.text: Raising verification from 10 to 20 years changes the 10-year assumption behind driver 1, not the driver's kind; saved status, dependencies, OCSP line and bank key stay; the re-timestamp job runs more often.
